calculateExpiredDelegations(address).details: Can be used in tandem with writeNewCheckpointForExpiredDelegations() to      write a new checkpoint. params.delegatee_: The delegatee whose expirations should be calculated

clearAutoDelegate().details: Sets autoDelegate[msg.sender] to address(0) so future positions      created for this address will self-delegate by default.      Does NOT re-delegate existing positions — call delegate() per-position      or adapter.delegate(self) to also re-delegate existing positions.

delegate(uint256,address).details: Delegations take effect at the next hourly epoch boundary. The delegator's      voting power is moved to the delegatee and expires when the delegator's      lock expires. To self-delegate, pass the NFT owner's address as delegatee_.      External callers cannot pass address(0) — that path reverts with      InvalidDelegatee. The internal forfeit path (called by VeHemi) uses      address(0) to clean up delegations of burned positions.

params.delegatee_: The address that will receive this token's voting power (non-zero)
params.delegator_: The veHEMI NFT token ID to delegate from (caller must be the NFT owner)

delegateAllFor(address,address).details: Can only be called by the trusted adapter, which passes through the      real msg.sender as the owner parameter. Expired locks are silently      skipped (they have zero voting power). Sets autoDelegate[owner_] so      future locks created for this owner auto-delegate to delegatee_.

params.delegatee_: The address to delegate all voting power to
params.owner_: The NFT owner whose positions should be delegated

params.delegator_: The token ID to delegate from (must be owned by msg.sender)
params.expiry: The time at which to expire the signature
params.nonce: The contract state required to match the signature
params.r: Half of the ECDSA signature pair
params.s: Half of the ECDSA signature pair
params.v: The recovery byte of the signature

eip712Domain().details: returns the fields and values that describe the domain separator used by this contract for EIP-712 signature.

finalizeMigration().details: Called once, AFTER the legacy state import is complete and      BEFORE `veHemi.updateVoteDelegation(newVVD)` flips the pointer.      After this call, neither `importDelegationsFromLegacy` nor      `importAutoDelegatesFromLegacy` can ever run again, preventing      post-migration state injection that would corrupt the      `getPastVotes` history for snapshots taken after finalize.      Idempotent: a second call is a no-op. Does not emit on no-op.

params.delegatee_: The delegatee_ to get checkpoints for

If the `clock()` is configured to use block numbers, this will return the value at the end of the corresponding block. NOTE: This value is the sum of all available votes, which is not necessarily the sum of all delegated votes. Votes that have not been delegated are still part of total supply, even though they would not participate in a vote.

params.timestamp_: The timestamp to check voting power at (must not be in the future)

returns._totalVotes: The voting power at the given timestamp

params.account_: The account to check voting power for

returns._0: The current voting power (includes both self votes and delegated votes)

importAutoDelegatesFromLegacy(address,ad.details: Owner enumeration must happen off-chain (no on-chain owner      registry). Operators typically derive the owners set from the      ERC721 transfer history of the VeHemi NFT.

params.legacy_: The OLD VeHemiVoteDelegation contract to read from.
params.owners_: Pagination cursor — owner addresses to migrate.

importDelegationsFromLegacy(address,uint.details: Each (tokenId, delegatee) is replayed via the normal `_delegate`      flow so checkpoint history begins building forward from this      block. Historical `getPastVotes` queries against this contract      for blocks BEFORE the import return zero — that is a fundamental      limitation of the pointer-swap model. Operators should schedule      the migration during a governance freeze (no in-flight      proposals) to avoid bricking active proposals.      Why not bypass `_delegate`? Replaying via `_delegate`:        (a) emits the standard `DelegateChanged` + `DelegateVotesChanged`            events so indexers see the import as ordinary delegation;        (b) re-runs the same slope/bias math used by future updates,            so the resulting checkpoint state is byte-identical to            what a fresh `delegate()` call would produce; (c) keeps            this function's storage-write surface tiny — the heavy            lifting lives in `_delegate`.

params.legacy_: The OLD VeHemiVoteDelegation contract to read from.                 MUST be non-zero. No check that it's the contract                 currently pointed at by `veHemi.voteDelegation()`,                 since this contract typically runs the import                 BEFORE the pointer swap.
params.tokenIds_: Pagination cursor — token IDs to replay. Caller is                 responsible for enumeration; operator should run                 this function repeatedly in chunks until the full                 set is covered.

refreshVotingPower(address).details: This function writes no state. It exists so that off-chain indexers (e.g. Aragon's subgraph) can be informed of voting-power decay between checkpoints. Anyone can call it (permissionless). Both previousVotes and newVotes in the emitted event are set to the current decayed power. This signals "the authoritative power is now X" without implying any delegation change occurred. This does NOT duplicate writeNewCheckpointForExpiredDelegations, which writes a new checkpoint to reflect expired delegations in storage. This function is purely for event emission.

params.delegatee_: The delegatee whose voting power to refresh

refreshVotingPowerBatch(address[]).details: Iterates over the array and calls refreshVotingPower for each. The caller is responsible for keeping the array length within gas limits.

params.delegatees_: Array of delegatee addresses to refresh

setAutoDelegate(address).details: Companion to `delegateAllFor` for users with too many positions      to fit a single bulk-delegate call within a block. Idempotent:      a no-op call (delegatee_ unchanged) returns without an SSTORE      or event emission.

params.delegatee_: The address future positions should auto-delegate to.        Pass `address(0)` to clear (equivalent to `clearAutoDelegate`).

setTrustedAdapter(address).details: Non-zero adapters MUST have non-empty bytecode (`code.length > 0`),         else the call reverts `InvalidAdapter`. The notify relays         (`notifyVotesChanged` / `notifyDelegateChanged`) are wrapped in         try/catch and a CALL to a zero-code address returns success         with empty data, so an EOA configured here would silently drop         every relay; the explicit code-length check surfaces the         misconfiguration at set time.         `address(0)` is preserved as an explicit disable; consumers         can monitor `TrustedAdapterUpdated(_, address(0))` to         distinguish a deliberate teardown from a typo. A staticcall         liveness probe of the candidate would always fail against a         conforming adapter because `notifyVotesChanged` emits a log         and `LOG*` is forbidden inside a STATICCALL.

params.adapter_: The adapter address (or address(0) to disable).

writeNewCheckpointForExpiredDelegations(.details: Long time periods between checkpoints can increase gas costs for subsequent      delegate() calls because the catch-up walk must iterate more SIX_DAYS      expiration buckets. Anyone can call this to amortize that cost.

CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL.details: Delegation checkpoints land on hour boundaries to give a responsive      governance UX while preventing same-block flash-delegation.

DELEGATION_TYPEHASH.details: Includes a `uint256 delegator` (tokenId) field — veHEMI's         delegation is per-tokenId, not account-wide, so a signer         authorizes the redelegation of ONE specific NFT. This         diverges from OpenZeppelin's canonical IVotes Delegation         hash (`Delegation(address delegatee,uint256 nonce,uint256         expiry)`); tooling assuming the OZ shape will produce digests         that fail verification here. Integrators wanting an account-         wide signed flow should issue per-tokenId signatures in a         batch. See `VeHemiAragonAdapter.delegateBySig`, which is         declared but reverts for the same reason.

MONTH.details: SIX_DAYS is the week-ish expiration bucket that must match VeHemi's      rounding grid exactly: YEAR / 60 = 525,960 seconds ≈ 6.0875 days.      MONTH is only used as an intermediate to make that division explicit.
